evidence_kinds.a: saved algorithmic reason from CV37 v3 (unchanged records)
evidence_kinds.b: offline deterministic replay diagnostics on the same saved frames
evidence_kinds.c: AI development observation of contact sheets (Claude observers + one skeptical cross-check); not human truth

method.frames: 625 saved frames / 10 pitches, 6-frame stride (0.1001 s); each pitch's first loss and the tiles around it
method.contact_sheets: seed tile plus loss-6..loss+3 tiles; cyan box = tracker 21 px template, orange circle = saved AI point; 4x zoom of 160 px around the last tracked point
method.cross_check: one skeptical agent re-read the loss and pre-loss tiles at 3x and could correct the primary category; corrections are recorded, not hidden
method.no_new_calls: no new video, paid service, mass AI reading or model training; the saved 325 readings were not re-called

skeptic_coverage_notes: Minor, not a criterion gap: 5:6 states 26802 was seen on the overview only; 3:3 states 17395/17407/17443 were seen on the full sheet only. Neither is the loss or pre-loss tile.

Category-consistency note for the record: the same 'tracker was on the bare hand' situation was labelled by loss mechanism in 3:1 (drift primary, seed identity secondary) and by root cause in 3:3 (seed identity primary); the 3:3 verdict above applies the mechanism rule. 5:1 is kept as seed_identity_uncertain because the seeded object is genuinely unidentifiable (dissolve-blended).

It changes shape frame to frame (rounded at 14946, elongated with a lighter tip at 14952, fingers pointing up-left at 14970/14976) while staying in place, which is most consistent with the catcher's bare right hand giving signs. Not a mitt pocket; not glove lacing; not shin guard, uniform or dirt. Identity not verified (a tan-leather portion of a glove cannot be fully excluded from the sheet).
c_ai_development_observation.mitt_at_loss_relative_to_tracked_point: Saved AI mitt reading at the loss frame is (642,242): ~18 px to the viewer's right and ~7 px above the tracked point (624,249), 19.3 px away. On the sheet it lands on the dark navy rounded object immediately to the viewer's right of the tracked tan blob (the catcher's left-hand side); that dark object, with a white patch at its right edge, is the visible candidate mitt. It is adjacent to, not covering, the tracked patch. By 14970 the AI reading has moved further right to (656,239), ~32 px from the tracked point, onto a white round patch on that object, while the tan blob stays where it was.
c_ai_development_observation.observer_evidence: Saved algorithmic reason: low_similarity at 14958, ncc 0.611 (< 0.65), peak_margin 0.103, appearance_change 0.003; previous confirmed step 14952 had ncc 0.819, margin 0.30, fb 0.0 at (624,249). Diagnostics at the loss frame: seed template best 0.611 at exactly the last tracked point (dist 0.0) at both r24 and r40, so the patch was not out of range and did not move; last confirmed patch matches 0.759 at (625,248), dist 1.4, margin 0.23; last_patch_vs_seed_template_ncc 0.819. The object is still in place and still matches its most recent appearance well, but its match to the fixed seed template fell from 0.82 to 0.61 in six frames: appearance drift against a fixed template. Visually the tracked blob is a small warm-toned hand-like object that is articulating in place (sign-giving), which explains the drift; no cut, no zoom/pan, no occluder over it at 14958, and the same camera framing in all six tiles. Secondary: the seed sits on this warm-toned blob on the catcher's bare-hand side, while the AI mitt readings at 14958 (642,242) and 14970 (656,239) are 19-32 px to the viewer's right on a distinct dark navy object with a white patch; seed-template NCC near the 14958 AI point is only 0.333, so the tracked patch and the AI-reported mitt are different-looking things. Tertiary note: 0.611 is only 0.039 under the 0.65 gate with a clear 0.10 margin, so threshold_borderline also applies. Mitt identity of either object is not verified; colour sampling of the un-annotated 14964 tile gives the blob a mean RGB of about (188,152,144) (warm, R>G>B) versus (84,81,96) for the adjacent dark object.

skeptic_cross_check.reason: Re-read 14946/14952/14958/14964 at 3x: the cyan patch is a flesh-toned rounded object that shows fingers at 14952 and 14964 (bare-hand-like), with a dark object bearing a white patch immediately to the viewer's right where the 14958 and 14970 AI circles land, so not_mitt is what the sheet shows. c_ai_development_observation.mitt_at_loss_relative_to_tracked_point: Saved AI reading at 16286 is [640,251]: 30 px left and 12 px below the last tracked point [670,239] (32.3 px). On the sheet, however, that orange circle sits on a light tan rounded object at the viewer's left between the catcher's knees (looks like the bare right hand, not verified). The dark rounded object with the white mark that the tracker had been following (catcher's left-hand side, viewer's right) appears roughly 10-15 px below and slightly left of the last tracked point at 16286, now lowered and turned compared with 16280; at 16292-16298 that same dark object sits near [676-680, 250-259] and the 16298 AI reading [680,259] is on it. c_ai_development_observation.observer_evidence: Saved algorithmic reason: low_similarity, ncc 0.395, margin 0.028. Visual: same centre-field framing on every tile (Truist Park sign, batter and pitcher unchanged) so no cut/zoom; nothing covers the tracked point (umpire's leg stays to the right). Between 16280 and 16286 the catcher drops from a high set-up (mitt presented as a target, white mark facing camera) into the low receiving crouch; torso bottom moves ~16 px down and the dark mitt-like object drops ~10-15 px and rotates. Quality trend while tracking: ncc 0.92 (16268) -> 0.81 (16274) -> 0.70 (16280) -> 0.39 (16286), a steady decay as the object turned, and last_patch_vs_seed_template_ncc is already 0.696 at the last confirmed frame. Second peak (0.367) is close in score but both are noise-level, so ambiguity is a symptom not a cause. AI displacement 32.3 px exceeds the 24 px radius, supporting fast motion, but that AI reading appears to sit on a tan object different from the seeded dark object, so it is weak evidence; the seed AI point coincided exactly with the tracked object and the 16274 AI point was 6 px away, so seed identity is not the issue. Threshold is not borderline (0.395 vs 0.65).

skeptic_cross_check.reason: Seed 16262: dark round object with a white mark on the viewer's-right (catcher's left) side, AI coincident, tan bare hand visible at the viewer's left; at 16286 the catcher has dropped into the crouch, the dark object sits ~10-15 px below the last point and rotated, and the AI jumps 32 px onto the tan hand. Seed template finds nothing within r40 (0.41) and the last patch only 0.551, so this is an abrupt pose/appearance change rather than gradual drift, but appearance change is the category the numbers support; not out-of-range (object within ~15 px) and nothing covers the point. Supported with that qualification.
